thread:
Ajay: Quick sync - paired with SRE on enqueue/batcher tradeoffs. Need RFC follow-up.
Taylor: summary please?
Ajay: Options: 1) edge enqueue + shard-aware central batcher, 2) centralized enqueue + scheduler, 3) hybrid: edge tags only. Tradeoffs: latency, ops surface, attribution correctness.
Maria: main failure modes?
Ajay: Hotspot/backpressure at edge, stripped attrs from edge minify, batch re-order across time windows.
Devin: Also loss of join keys if edge compacts envelopes.
Taylor: Edge prefix-caching reduces central load (~30% peak win) but caused ~5s attribution skew during churn.
Maria: Regulated tenants can't accept skew - opt-in caching per tenant?
Ajay: Proposal: tenant opt-in + canonical header from edge (X-RW-CANONICAL). Central honors header if enabled, otherwise full enrich. Migration: observe -> compare -> promote.
ops-bot: Canary deploy: ingest-edge v2 -> 2026-04-02 03:00 UTC, 10% traffic.
Taylor: Time-window invariants?
Ajay: Declare: "batcher must preserve event_time monotonicity per tenant". Add seq-num per tenant+stream and include first_event_ts,last_event_ts in batch envelope for stitching.
Devin: Seq-num cost small (+~12B/event) but gives determinism.
Maria: Cross-region fallback: require identical canonicalization lib in all regions and include region_id in metadata to debug mismatches.
Taylor: RBAC: Platform toggles opt-ins; product requests via onboarding; must audit every toggle.
Devin: Add a sampling probe (1/10k) that compares canonical vs enrich output to feed regression alerts and Optimize signals.
Ajay: I'll update RFC follow-up: invariants, opt-in flow, seq numbers, audit events, sampling probe. Ping to add appendix with experiment numbers. End.
